Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit and rejoinder affidavit filed by the applicant are taken on record.
2. Heard learned counsel for the accused-applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as Shri Sushil Kumar, learned counsel for the complainant/informant and perused the record.

3. This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Abhinav Singh for grant of bail, in Case Crime No. 35 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. & Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Vikas Nagar, District Lucknow, during trial.
4. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that it is a case of false implication.
The applicant is the husband of the deceased who has committed suicide just after three months of her marriage with the applicant.
However, at the relevant night, the applicant was not accompanying the deceased as a night before the applicant and the deceased had Abhinav Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru.

1 quarreled on account of the fact that the deceased was pressurizing the applicant to live separately from his parents.

5. It is further submitted that when he awoke in the morning, he noticed the dead body of the deceased hanging in her room, while he had slept in the room of his mother and he immediately informed the concerned police station and also to the family members of the deceased.

6. It is vehemently submitted that perusal of the post-mortem and the inquest report would fortify that the deceased had committed suicide, however, later on, at the instance of other persons, an FIR has been lodged by the informant alleging cruelty in lieu of demand of dowry.

It is also submitted that during the course of the trial, the statement of the informant namely, Jitendra Verma has been recorded and though he was intact in his chief examination, however, during the course of his cross examination, he stated that the deceased has never made any complaint to her pertaining to commission of cruelty in lieu of any demand of dowry and in fact, he has not written the FIR which in fact was written by his cousin and as he was disturbed, he did not read what had been written therein.
7.

It is vehemently submitted that the informant, who is the brother of the deceased, has not supported the version of the prosecution and has stated the real facts and, therefore, the further detention of the applicant in prison would not reap any fruits as he is already in jail since 28.2.2023 and the culmination of the trial would take a long time having regard to the number of witnesses cited in the charge-sheet.
8. It is next submitted that the applicant is not having any criminal history.
Charge sheet in this case has already been filed and there is no apprehension that after being released on bail he may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.

9. Learned A.G.A. opposes the prayer for bail of the applicant on the ground that the applicant is the husband of the deceased and during the course of investigation, there was ample evidence against the applicant.
Thus, he is not entitled to be released on bail.
10. Shri Sushil Kumar, learned counsel for the informant/complainant submits that he does not want to say anything in the matter.

11. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is reflected that the applicant is the husband of the deceased who had died within a very short time of her marriage with the applicant.

The cause of death of the deceased as has been ascertained in the post-mortem,
is asphyxia as a result of ante-mortem hanging.

Two minor injuries of the nature of contusion have also been found around the neck of the deceased, but in all probability, the same may only be related with the ligature marks or the attempts made by the deceased to commit suicide.

There is a GD entry of police station concerned, a copy of which has been placed on record, wherein a written information pertaining to the death of the deceased given by the applicant has been recorded and it has been mentioned therein that in the night, a quarrel had taken place between the applicant and the deceased, as the deceased was insisting him to live separately and the applicant had gone to Abhinav Singh vs State Of U.P. 2 sleep in the room belonging to his mother and in the morning, he had seen the dead body of the deceased hanging in her room.
It is also evident that the informant, who is the brother of the deceased, was intact in the chief examination, however, has resiled from his statement in the cross examination.
The applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 28.2.2023 without any criminal history.
Charge sheet in this case has also been filed and the presence of the applicant may be secured before the trial court by placing adequate conditions.

12. Thus, having regard to all the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in eye on the period of detention of the applicant in this case, a case of bail is made out in favour of the applicant.
Thus, the bail application is allowed.

13. Let the accused/applicant- Abhinav Singh involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
14.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
15. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
16. Observations made herein-above by this court are only for the purpose of disposal of this bail application and shall not be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
